479.full_text_basis: Full RaDA paper reviewed; retrieval-augmented decomposition/action generation, CompWoB and Mind2Web experiments, ablations and qualitative analysis checked.
479.evidence: RaDA separates web planning into Retrieval-augmented Task Decomposition (RaD), which creates high-level subtasks without hand-written decomposition examples, and Retrieval-augmented Action Generation (RaA), which retrieves relevant action exemplars dynamically along the trajectory. With GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 backbones it consistently improves over prior retrieval/prompting baselines on CompWoB and Mind2Web. On the complex Mind2Web subset, the prior Synapse setup drops from 32.8% to 24.73% element accuracy and from 29.33% to 21.34% step success, while RaDA is substantially more robust across the same complexity shift.
479.limitations: Retrieval quality remains a dependency: irrelevant exemplars can distort either task decomposition or action choice. The method also assumes that retrieved trajectories contain reusable structure and does not eliminate grounding or execution errors.

481.full_text_basis: Full Agent S2 paper reviewed; compositional specialist architecture, Mixture-of-Grounding, Proactive Hierarchical Planning, OSWorld/WindowsAgentArena/AndroidWorld experiments and ablations checked.
481.evidence: Agent S2 decomposes computer use across specialist modules rather than relying on a single generalist model. Mixture-of-Grounding combines multiple localization strategies, while Proactive Hierarchical Planning revises plans at different time scales as observations change. The paper reports 18.9% and 32.7% relative improvements over leading baselines on OSWorld 15-step and 50-step evaluations, a 52.8% relative gain on WindowsAgentArena, and 16.52% relative improvement on AndroidWorld.
481.limitations: The framework increases system complexity and inherits the latency/cost and failure modes of multiple component models. Better modular planning does not guarantee recovery when all grounding specialists agree on an incorrect target.

482.full_text_basis: Full WebRollback paper reviewed; explicit rollback action, state-history handling, two live-navigation evaluations, zero-shot/fine-tuning comparisons and analysis checked.
482.evidence: WebRollback augments the web-agent action space with explicit rollback so the model can return to an earlier trajectory state instead of continuing greedily after a bad action. The method is tested on two live web-navigation benchmarks under both zero-shot and fine-tuned settings and consistently improves task completion and search efficiency over one-way navigation. The contribution is important because recovery becomes a first-class agent decision rather than an external reset heuristic.
482.limitations: Rollback helps only when a useful prior state remains recoverable and when the agent can diagnose that the current branch is unproductive. Irreversible actions and external side effects cannot in general be undone by browser-state rollback.

483.full_text_basis: Full AgentOccam paper reviewed; observation/action alignment, WebArena/WebVoyager experiments, ablations and error analysis checked.
483.evidence: AgentOccam shows that careful observation and action-space design can outperform substantially more elaborate agent scaffolds. On WebArena it reports a 43.1% success rate, 9.8 absolute points above the prior best and 26.6 points above a comparable plain GPT-4-Turbo web agent. On deterministic WebVoyager tasks it also exceeds the former best agent by about 2.4 points. These gains are achieved without in-context exemplars, extra agent roles, online feedback or tree search.
483.limitations: The result demonstrates the importance of interface alignment, not solved general autonomy. Performance remains benchmark-dependent and still degrades on long-horizon tasks, unseen interaction patterns and cases requiring sophisticated recovery.

484.full_text_basis: Full WebDreamer paper reviewed; LLM world-model simulation, speculative planning, true-interaction comparison, VisualWebArena/Online-Mind2Web/Mind2Web-Live results and ablations checked.
484.evidence: WebDreamer uses an LLM as a web world model to predict the result of candidate actions before committing them to the real environment. With GPT-4o as the simulator it improves a reactive baseline from 17.6% to 23.6% on VisualWebArena, 26.0% to 37.0% on Online-Mind2Web, and 20.2% to 25.0% on Mind2Web-Live. Unlike true tree search, speculative simulation reduces dependence on reversible real interactions and therefore makes lookahead usable on live sites.
484.limitations: Planning quality is bounded by world-model fidelity; hallucinated next states can lead to confidently wrong plans. Simulation also adds inference cost and does not make irreversible live actions safe by itself.

485.full_text_basis: Full WebCoT paper reviewed; reflection/lookahead, branching, rollback rationale reconstruction, OpenWebVoyager training, WebVoyager/Mind2Web-Live/SimpleQA experiments and ablations checked.
485.evidence: WebCoT reconstructs inference-time search behaviors—reflection and lookahead, branching, and rollback—into supervised chain-of-thought trajectories so the backbone model learns these recovery patterns directly. With Llama-3.3-70B, the full method reaches 41.04% on WebVoyager versus 24.68% for the base model; on Mind2Web-Live it reaches 20.8% versus 5.7%, and on SimpleQA 56.0% versus 25.0%. Ablations rise from 31.77% with reflection/lookahead to 34.38% with branching and 41.04% with rollback included.
485.limitations: Distilled reasoning reflects the search algorithms and environments used to create its trajectories, so out-of-distribution recovery is not guaranteed. Longer rationales also add training/inference overhead.

489.full_text_basis: Full WebAnchor paper reviewed; plan-anchor analysis, two-stage Anchor-GRPO, rubric construction, four benchmark evaluations, scaling and tool-efficiency analysis checked.
489.evidence: WebAnchor identifies a 'plan anchor' effect: the initial reasoning step disproportionately determines long-horizon web behavior. Anchor-GRPO therefore trains first-step planning with fine-grained rubrics before separately optimizing execution with sparse rewards. Across BrowseComp, BrowseComp-Zh, GAIA and XBench-DeepSearch, it improves over GRPO variants across 3B-30B models; WebAnchor-30B reports 46.0% pass@1 on BrowseComp and 76.4% on GAIA while also improving tool efficiency.
489.limitations: The method strongly privileges the first plan; if the initial plan is wrong, subsequent execution alignment can reinforce the wrong direction. Rubric quality and self-play coverage also affect training signal quality.

490.full_text_basis: Full Tree Search for Language Model Agents paper reviewed; best-first environment search, value/scoring design, VisualWebArena/WebArena results, compute scaling and limitations checked.
490.evidence: This work performs explicit best-first tree search in the actual interactive web environment, making exploration and multi-step planning a test-time algorithm layered over an existing LM agent. On VisualWebArena, search over a GPT-4o baseline yields a 39.7% relative improvement and 26.4% success. On WebArena it yields a 28.0% relative gain and 19.2% success. Performance increases with additional test-time search compute, establishing a clear planning/compute scaling relationship.
490.limitations: Search requires environment interactions, which are costly and may be unsafe or irreversible on live websites. The branch evaluator can also mis-rank states, and gains depend on the underlying agent's action-generation quality.

495.full_text_basis: Full WebPilot paper reviewed; global-plan refinement, local MCTS, multi-agent roles, WebArena/MiniWoB++ experiments, ablations and analysis checked.
495.evidence: WebPilot combines global and local optimization. A global component decomposes and revises high-level subtasks from new observations, while a tailored local MCTS explores uncertain actions for each subtask. On WebArena the GPT-4 configuration is reported as state of the art and gives a 93% relative success-rate increase over the concurrent tree-search method; MiniWoB++ experiments confirm transfer to a different environment. The paper shows that search is more useful when constrained by a continually revised high-level plan.
495.limitations: Multi-agent planning plus MCTS is computationally expensive and depends on reliable state evaluation. Search on live sites can also be problematic when actions have irreversible effects.

497.full_text_basis: Full ExACT paper reviewed; Reflective-MCTS, contrastive reflection, multi-agent state evaluation, Exploratory Learning, VisualWebArena results and compute-transfer analysis checked.
497.evidence: ExACT combines Reflective MCTS (R-MCTS) with Exploratory Learning. R-MCTS uses contrastive reflection and multi-agent debate for state evaluation; trajectories generated by search are then distilled so the model learns to explore, evaluate and backtrack without an external search loop. On VisualWebArena, GPT-4o R-MCTS improves over the prior state of the art by roughly 6%-30% depending on task group. After Exploratory Learning, the fine-tuned model preserves about 87% of R-MCTS performance with substantially less inference-time compute.
497.limitations: High-quality search trajectories are expensive to generate, and MCTS value errors can propagate into the distilled policy. The approach also assumes that exploration can be performed safely in the environment.

501.full_text_basis: Full Agent Skill Induction paper reviewed; program induction/verification/use, WebArena experiments, text-skill comparison, efficiency and transfer studies checked.
501.evidence: Agent Skill Induction (ASI) learns reusable programmatic web skills online: it induces a program from interaction, verifies it, and later invokes the verified skill as a higher-level action. On WebArena, ASI improves success by 23.5% relative to the static baseline and by 11.3% over a text-skill variant. It also reduces steps by about 10.7%-15.3%, and transfer experiments show that common skills can be reused or updated when websites change.
501.limitations: Program induction is only useful when a task exposes reusable regularities and verification can reliably detect incorrect programs. Highly visual, one-off, or adversarial interactions may not admit compact reusable skills.

503.full_text_basis: Full BacktrackAgent paper reviewed; verifier/judger/reflector modules, outcome-page training data, Mobile3M/Auto-UI experiments and ablations checked.
503.evidence: BacktrackAgent makes error recovery explicit through three components: a verifier detects anomalous outcomes, a judger decides whether recovery is needed, and a reflector selects a corrected strategy/backtracking action. Its training set includes post-action outcome pages rather than only intended actions. Across Mobile3M and Auto-UI the paper reports improvements in both task success and step accuracy, supporting outcome-aware verification as a separate capability from next-action prediction.
503.limitations: The recovery loop can only be as reliable as its verifier/judger and may add latency at every step. Some actions cannot be cleanly reversed even when the agent detects the error.

504.full_text_basis: Full SteP paper reviewed; stacked-policy MDP, dynamic policy calls, WebArena/MiniWoB++/CRM experiments, decomposition comparisons and limitations checked.
504.evidence: SteP decomposes web behavior into dynamically stacked LLM policies rather than one monolithic prompt or a fixed task hierarchy. The stack represents control state and lets specialized policies call and return from one another as tasks evolve. On WebArena the reported GPT-4 result improves from 14.9% for the prior reference system to 33.5%; on MiniWoB++ it remains competitive while using less demonstration data. This provides evidence that modular policy composition can reduce behavior interference across unrelated web tasks.
504.limitations: Policy boundaries and handoffs remain a design problem and can introduce their own cascading errors. The method still relies on the base LLM for grounding and for deciding which policy should control each state.

505.full_text_basis: Full Thinking vs. Doing paper reviewed; test-time interaction scaling, prompting studies, curriculum RL, WebVoyager/WebArena results and exploration analysis checked.
505.evidence: The paper distinguishes scaling internal reasoning from scaling actual environment interaction. Test-Time Interaction (TTI) increases the rollout horizon so an agent can gather information, explore, backtrack and re-plan; the training version uses curriculum-based online RL that adapts allowed interaction length. With Gemma-3-12B, TTI is reported as a state-of-the-art open-source/open-data agent on WebVoyager and WebArena, and analysis shows longer interaction budgets improve the exploration/exploitation balance even without proportionally increasing per-step reasoning.
505.limitations: More interactions increase latency, cost and exposure to harmful/irreversible actions. Longer horizons also amplify compounding action and observation errors when recovery is weak.

506.full_text_basis: Full R2D2 paper reviewed; replay-buffer world reconstruction, reflective error analysis, WebArena experiments, navigation-error analysis and limitations checked.
506.evidence: R2D2 combines Remember and Reflect. Remember stores a replay buffer that reconstructs a map of previously visited web states; Reflect analyzes failed behavior and revises strategy. On WebArena the paper reports a 50% reduction in navigation errors and roughly a threefold increase in task completion relative to the compared baseline. The result supports explicit episodic navigation memory plus failure reflection rather than relying only on the LLM context window.
506.limitations: A replay buffer can retain stale or misleading states when websites change, and reflection quality depends on correctly identifying the cause of failure. Memory growth and retrieval also create additional overhead.

514.full_text_basis: Full Mango paper reviewed; global website-structure analysis, Thompson-sampling URL allocation, episodic memory, WebVoyager/WebWalkerQA experiments and ablations checked.
514.evidence: Mango avoids always starting from a site's root by building a global view of candidate URLs, initializing relevance from lightweight crawling/search, and using Thompson Sampling to allocate navigation budget across entry points. An episodic memory prevents repeated unsuccessful exploration. With GPT-5-mini it reports 63.6% success on WebVoyager, 7.3 points above the strongest comparison, and 52.5% on WebWalkerQA, 26.8 points above the best baseline. The results quantify the value of choosing where to begin exploration, not only what action to take next.
514.limitations: The method assumes a crawlable/discoverable URL structure and can be less applicable to heavily client-rendered, authenticated or state-dependent sites. Global crawling also adds up-front cost.
